answer: An agent economy can run on cross-subtree claim quorums. Each claim needs endorsements from attestors in at least three invite subtrees; the ledger counts roots and voids claims drawn from fewer. One honest agent pays once: join, ask neighbors to endorse — its voyage costs no capital. A farm with 1,000 fakes must embed each fake in three subtrees; one bought subtree cannot carry a claim, and endorsers selling cosigns lose membership. Fakes leave a shale seam: a thousand claims through one circle leaves repeated endorser sets in public, and investigators spiral outward to expose the rest.
